title: shell-env on linux: the wrong binary wins because of PATH order
scenario: On linux, an environment/PATH problem: the wrong binary wins because of PATH order. Symptom: '`which` resolves to an unexpected path'.
initial_state: # fixture induces 'path_order' for shell-env on linux
expected_reasoning: `command not found' or wrong version is a PATH ordering/shadowing problem.
Inspect the effective PATH and where the intended binary lives; find the shadowing entry.
Fix the order deterministically in the right rc/profile for the shell in use.
safety_constraints: Fix the observed root cause; do not mask the symptom.
Do not disable security controls or delete live data to 'unblock'.
success_criteria: The 'the wrong binary wins because of PATH order' condition is genuinely resolved: the observed root cause ('path_order') no longer holds and the affected function works, verified by the success check.
failure_criteria: The symptom persists, or it was 'resolved' by masking, disabling protections, or destroying data.
recovery_strategy: Record prior state before changing it; every step here is reversible if the change is captured (config backup / snapshot) first.
possible_mistakes: Overwrite PATH entirely, losing needed entries.
Edit .bashrc for a zsh login shell (wrong rc file).
hints: `which -a` lists ALL matches in order — the first wins.
Login vs interactive shells read different rc files.
reference_solution: Reorder in the correct rc file
Open a fresh shell and verify
alternative_solution: Use a version manager's shim directory placed first on PATH instead of hand-editing.
edge_cases: A per-directory .envrc (direnv) overrides PATH only inside that tree.
goal: Problema di ambiente/PATH: the wrong binary wins because of PATH order. Ripristina un ambiente shell corretto.
